# GTA 6 clips channel: research and build plan

Written 14 November 2026. One file with everything: what the research found, what was built on
branch `clp`, and what is left for you to do.

**How to read this.** Section 1 is the summary; if you read one thing, read that. Section 2 is the
build. Sections 3 to 5 are the research behind both: 27 sections, each written by one researcher and
then checked by two independent fact-checkers (one against primary sources, one for whether it is
still true and realistic for a new channel). Every fact carries an id such as (money-6) that points
to its row in that section's findings table, with the source and the checkers' verdict. Where a
claim could not be confirmed, it says "(unverified)". Nothing here is legal advice.

**What is in it**

1. Summary: what the research says and what we are building
2. The build plan: what is on branch `clp`
3. Research on GTA 6 and gaming footage (sections G1 to G8)
4. Research on YouTube, clips channels and the code we have (sections A1 to A12)
5. Answers to the gaps a critic found (sections A13 onward)

Sections A1 to A12 were written before it was clear that the subject is GTA 6, so their examples are
about interview and podcast clips; what they say about YouTube's rules, limits and tools still
applies. Section A4 lists source channels for a different niche: only its way of vetting a channel
is useful. Where a G section and an A section disagree about GTA or gaming, the G section wins; where
a gap section and an earlier section disagree, the gap section is newer and wins.

## 1. Summary: what the research says and what we are building

### The short answer

A channel of other creators' GTA 6 clips, posted without permission, should be planned as earning $0 from YouTube ads. YouTube refuses to pay for "promotion of other people's content (even if you have permission)", its Shorts pool drops re-uploads, and a streamer's consented clips channel was reported on 28 September 2026 as removed from the Partner Programme (the operator is appealing) (G2 money-6, money-11, money-13). The route also puts the channel at risk. Credit is no defence, each clip can bring a manual takedown and a strike, and 3 copyright strikes put the channel up for termination. A terminated person may not use any other channel they run or appear in, so by the text of the rules the company channel is exposed too (A3 policy-1, policy-5; A13 gap1-1).

Even your own gameplay has no written right to earn ads. Rockstar's policy, as read once through a text reader, tolerates only non-commercial fan use, and Take-Two's terms bar commercial use without separate written terms, so all GTA ad income rests on Take-Two's tolerance (G3 grules-2, grules-5, grules-7). The route that can earn over time is a long-form-led channel of GTA 6 footage someone records, with a real person's commentary, posted slowly (G2 money-9, money-22; G3 grules-21). Even that route will most likely earn little or nothing for months. From 1 February 2027 a new channel needs 8,000 watch hours in a year or 20M Shorts views in 90 days to join the Partner Programme, so ad money is months away at best (G2 money-2). From the same date, Shorts ad money needs 10M Shorts views every 90 days, which a new channel should not expect to reach (G2 money-3; G3 grules-m7). The fastest honest dollar is a paid clipping campaign, but the one GTA 6 campaign pays $0.70 per 1,000 views on TikTok and Instagram only (G2 money-15). Posting every hour does not help: no source rewards volume, sub-hour gaps went with far fewer views in vendor data, and an hourly templated feed is the pattern YouTube's spam and "inauthentic content" rules name (A1 growth-12; G4 gsrc-m2).

So we are building a "clips" system that posts only footage with a rights record: own capture, written permission, a creator's public permission, a clipping campaign, Creative Commons, or official material used inside Rockstar's policy. The no-permission route you chose is not built. The system finds new videos from approved sources, picks moments, renders Shorts and longer clips with ffmpeg, and queues them for your ten-minute daily approval on a small web page. Approved clips are uploaded private with a publish time. It starts at 1 post a day and climbs to at most 6, at least 3 hours apart. It runs on its own small AWS server with its own data folder, Google account, Cloud project and sign-in, and a guard refuses any channel but the clips channel. Today it has nothing it is allowed to post, so it needs you to choose a footage source this week: either buy a console and find someone who plays and talks, or get a written yes from creators.

### Your ideas, tested

| Idea | What the evidence says | Verdict | What to do instead |
|---|---|---|---|
| Clip other GTA 6 creators without permission ("edit and credit") | Credit and disclaimers give no rights (A3 policy-5). YouTube asks for "explicit written permission" for others' content (G3 grules-m9). Creators can remove each clip with a strike; Content ID money goes to the claimant (G2). Kick's terms bar copying and editing others' content (G8 gingest-m3). The GTA 6 campaign page itself says not to pull other creators' clips (G2 money-m3). | Do not | Own capture with commentary; creator clips only after a written yes (G4 sample message) |
| Earn YouTube ad money from a clips-only channel | Reused-content rule applies "even if you have permission"; Shorts pool excludes re-uploads; no accepted gaming clips channel found; one consented channel reported removed, appeal pending (G2 money-6, money-11, money-13) | Do it differently | A fan channel of own gameplay with real commentary, long-form first; ads off until Take-Two replies or you choose to rely on tolerance (G3 guard 9) |
| Post every hour (24 a day) | Gaps under 1 h: median 7,978 views vs 24,022 at 24-48 h (vendor data, A1 growth-12). Small gaming channels earned 73% less per view at 5-8 videos a month than at 3-4 (correlation only, G2 money-10). Channel upload limit unpublished (A19). Hourly needs about 18 source hours of footage a day (G5 gpick-m9) | Do it differently | 1 a day, climb to at most 6, at least 3 h apart; hourly stays a setting (A1 point 1) |
| Post Shorts and long clips | Shorts-feed views do not count toward watch hours (G2 money-1). One studied clips channel posts one 10-30 min cut a day; that is a single anecdote (A2 clips-13) | Do it | One long video of 8-20 min a week at first, plus 1 Short a day rising to 2-3, pointing to it; Shorts capped at 59 s (G1 points 6, 8; G6 glook-16) |
| Make the Shorts with ffmpeg | The app already has most pieces; four templates fit gameplay; 30 fps output, 1080x1920 (G6) | Do it | As built; benchmark render time first (G6 Risks) |

Per-Short Hyperframes renders are slow, have a silent missing-text bug, and no source links polish to views; rotating templates is itself a "template-based change" (A8 hf-15, hf-20, hf-m6) | Do it differently | Later, pre-render 2-3 stings once and lay them on with ffmpeg (A8 option c; G6 point 8) |
| A new channel separate from the company channel | Needed, but it does not protect the person: a terminated owner may not use any channel they run or appear in (A13 gap1-1, gap1-3). A GTA channel would almost certainly send no traffic to the company channel (our estimate, A17 gap5-10) | Do it | A separate Google account and Cloud project, so a bug can never post to the company channel. It does not shield you: the rule binds the person, so the real protection is posting only what has a rights record and stopping at the first strike (A13 point 2) |
| Run it on AWS 24/7 | Never on the production t3.large: shared 8 GB, no swap; a deploy restart abandons running jobs and can remove extra containers (A12 host-1, host-2). | Launch with the game on 19 November | 5 days away; no gameplay exists before then; pre-release and leaked footage is taken down and Take-Two filed court subpoenas to find a leaker (G1 gta-16; G3 grules-3, grules-9) | Do not | First upload about 26-29 November, full rhythm by about day 14 (G1 point 1) |
| Ten minutes a day to approve posts | Enough to approve. Not enough to make the content: commentary must come from a person, and own capture needs hours of play (G3 guard 7; G4 point 2) | Do it differently | Approvals stay with you; someone else plays and talks |

### What can earn, fastest first

1. **Paid clipping campaigns (Content Rewards, paid out through Whop).**
   - Needs: an account, clips on your own TikTok, Instagram or YouTube accounts as each brief says, and the ad disclosure the brief asks for (the GTA 6 brief wants it at the start of each clip).
   - Pays: the GTA 6 "Tokyo Girl" campaign promotes a song, not the game, and gives $0.70 per 1,000 views, $2 minimum and $35 maximum a clip, from a $2,000 budget with $88 used by 14 Nov 2026, on TikTok and Instagram only (G2 money-15). Named game-publisher campaigns pay $1.50-4.00 per 1,000; the range across 62 game campaigns is $0.90-20 (G4 gsrc-16; G2 money-16). The median across 712 campaigns was about $1.04 (A2 clips-9). Content Rewards keeps 10% on per-view campaigns (G2 money-17).
   - Time: the fastest first dollar of any route (G2). At 6,000 views a month and the $1.20 YouTube median it is about $7 a month (A2 clips-m12).
   - What stops it: small budgets and caps; some campaigns pay $0 for views from Pakistan, India and Bangladesh (G2 money-16, money-m8); footage is licensed only for that campaign (G2 money-m4); campaign clips are "promotion of other people's content", so they do not belong on the ad-earning channel (G2 money-11).
2. **YouTube ads on long videos of your own GTA 6 footage with commentary.**
   - Needs: from 1 Feb 2027, 8,000 watch hours in 365 days (1,000 subscribers is today's rule; YouTube's blog does not restate it for 2027); a review of about a month; AdSense (G2 money-1, money-2).
   - Pays: gaming long-form median $2.05 per 1,000 views, middle half $0.70-3.62, measured on already-monetised channels with 10,000+ subscribers (vendor data, G2 money-9). Advertisers pay only $0.20-1.50 per 1,000 ad views (CPM) for audiences in Nigeria, Pakistan or the Philippines (vendor data, G2 money-m6).
   - Time: many months. About 31% of new channels that added 52+ videos in a year reached 1,000 subscribers within that year (A2 clips-20).
   - What stops it: Take-Two's tolerance, not a licence (G3 grules-7); violence rules (no graphic violence in the thumbnail or first 7 s, no kill montages) (G2 money-12, money-m1); a failed review.
3. **YouTube Shorts ad share.**
   - Needs: from 1 Feb 2027, 10M qualified Shorts views in 90 days (G2 money-3).
   - Pays: $0.07-0.20 per 1,000 in most niches; the one gaming example is $0.17, from one channel (G2 money-8). YouTube's own manager said a few thousand views earn "a few cents" a month (G2 money-7).
   - Honest answer: plan on $0 for a new channel.
4. **Fan funding (memberships, Super Thanks).**
   - Needs: 500 subscribers, 3 public uploads in 90 days, and 3,000 hours or 3M Shorts views (G2 money-4).
   - Pays: no ad money at all, and Pakistan is not on its country list (G2 money-4).
5. **Routes that pay nothing.**
   - No-permission clips: ad money goes to the claimant or nowhere (G2 money-6).
   - Consented re-uploads with light edits (G2 money-13).
   - Traffic to the company channel from a GTA channel (A17 gap5-10).
   - Selling the channel: no rule found either way, and this point is unverified; do not plan on it (G2 money-19b).

### What the research asks of the build, and where the build stands

The research put seventeen requirements on the software. This is where each one stands on branch `clp`. "The reviewer" means you, during the daily ten minutes.

| # | The research asks for | Where the build stands |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | A rights record per source, or no clip (G3, G8, A3) | Built. Checked when a source is enabled, when its videos are listed, before a video is processed, and again right before an upload. There is no override. |
| 2 | The no-permission route is not built (G3 grules-21) | Built that way: a source with no rights basis can be listed but is never clipped. |
| 3 | A channel guard (A9, A11) | Built. Before every upload the signed-in channel must equal `CLIPS_CHANNEL_ID` and must not be on the refuse list. |
| 4 | Private upload with a publish time (A9, A12) | Built. A clip whose time has passed goes back for a new slot; nothing goes public at once. |
| 5 | Slow pace by default (A1, A19) | Built: 1 a day, at most 6, at least 3 hours apart. Not built: counting uploads you make by hand in Studio, and lowering the pace by itself after an upload-limit error (the error stops that upload and shows a plain message). |
| 6 | No story spoilers (G3, G5, G7) | Partly. The picker is told to avoid them and drops what it flags. The reviewer is the real check. There is no banned-word list for titles yet. |
| 7 | No licensed music (G3, G6) | Not built as a detector. The picker's flag only catches what titles and captions give away. The reviewer has to listen. |
| 8 | Nothing from before the release (G3, G7) | Built: a video dated before `CLIPS_NOT_BEFORE` (19 November 2026) is skipped, unless the source is official material. |
| 9 | Ad-safe opening (G2, G7) | Not built. The reviewer. |
| 10 | Real commentary by a person on every post (G3, A16) | Not built. The system cuts, frames and captions footage; it does not add a person's voice. This is the gap between "posts go out" and "posts can earn". |
| 11 | Your approval on every post (G1) | Built, on by default. |
| 12 | Stop on the first strike (A3, A13) | Partly. The breaker and the kill switch are built, but nothing reads YouTube's emails, so a person has to press the button or run `python -m clips kill`. |
| 13 | Ads off by default (G3) | Not a software matter: ads are switched on in YouTube Studio. |
| 14 | Separate everything (A9, A11, A14) | Built into the guards and the set-up guide: own data folder, own sign-in, own Cloud project, own server. |
| 15 | No downloading from YouTube without YouTube's permission (A3, A5) | Built as the default: `CLIPS_YOUTUBE_DOWNLOADS` is off, and files come from a watched folder. Switching it on is your decision. |
| 16 | Fan-channel identity (G7) | In the set-up guide. Every description carries the not-affiliated line. |
| 17 | Shorts of 59 seconds or less, 30 frames a second, 1080x1920 (G6) | Built (the cap is 58 seconds). |

### Decisions only you can make

1. **Where does the footage come from?**
   - Options: (a) buy a PS5 or Xbox Series, the game and a capture card, and have someone play and talk; (b) ask creators for a written yes; (c) clipping campaigns on separate accounts; (d) no permission.
   - Recommended: (a). It is the only source you fully control, and even the GTA 6 campaign page calls own console footage "the safest kind to use" (G4 gsrc-15; G8). (d) is not built.
   - Default: the build posts nothing until a source has a rights record.
2. **Turn ads on, and on what basis?**
   - Options: wait for a written reply from copyright@take2games.com, or record a choice to rely on Take-Two's tolerance.
   - Recommended: write first; it is the cheapest risk cut, and silence is not a yes (G3 grules-4; G4 gsrc-m12).
   - Default: ads off.
3. **Who runs the channel?**
   - Options: (a) you, with a system built never to get a strike; (b) another person with their own Google account, phone, ID and AdSense and no role on the company channel; (c) do not build.
   - Recommended: (a). The research says plainly that separate accounts cannot promise isolation, because the rules bind the person (A13 point 2).
   - Default: (a), with a full stop on the first strike.
4. **How fast to post?**
   - Options: stay at 1-3 a day, climb to 6, or set hourly.
   - Recommended: the slow ramp, raised only while views hold and no limit errors appear (A1 point 2; A19 point 1).
   - Default: 1 a day, cap 6, at least 3 h apart.
5. **How long to avoid story spoilers?**
   - Options: 2-3 weeks (G1), 30 days (G7) or 8 weeks (G5).
   - Recommended: the research does not agree; we suggest 8 weeks, the safest.
   - Default: spoilers dropped until you change the setting.
6. **Language.**
   - Options: English only, or later an Urdu or Hindi commentary channel as a separate product.
   - Recommended: English for the first 8 weeks, until analytics shows where viewers are (G7 point 10).
   - Default: English.
7. **Clipping campaigns as a side business?**
   - Options: run campaign clips on separate TikTok and Instagram accounts, or skip.
   - Recommended: keep them off this channel (G2 point 3; G4 point 9).
   - Default: not part of the channel's posting.
8. **AI account and model.**
   - Options: share the company's Anthropic organisation, or use a separate one; add Gemini or not.
   - Recommended: a separate organisation, or at least a workspace limit, because the $500 cap is shared and hitting it stops production's AI step (A12 host-18). Gemini only as a test (G5 Risks).
   - Default: Haiku for scans, Sonnet for re-rank and titles, with a daily spend cap.
9. **Server size.**
   - Options: t3.medium (about $37 a month, baseline 9.6 vCPU-hours a day) or t3.large ($61-70).
   - Recommended: start small and measure; a t3.medium can fall short at volume (A12 host-m14).
   - Default: as the build sets it. Check the credit mode before relying on it (A12 host-m12).
10. **Public repo.**
    - The repo is public, so the clips branch publishes its code, source list and schedule (A12 host-m19).
    - Options: accept that, or move clips to a private repo.
    - Recommended: private. Default: at your request the code and this file are pushed to the `clp` branch of the public repo; nothing is merged to `main`. The list of sources and the schedule live in the data folder, which is never in git.

### Your next seven days

1. **Sat 14 Nov - Sun 15 Nov: choose the footage route** (decision 1). If (a), find the person who will play and talk for at least a few hours a day, because hourly posting needs many hours of play (G4 point 2).
2. **Sun 15 Nov: read the rules yourself.** Open Rockstar's "Policy on posting copyrighted Rockstar Games material" (support.rockstargames.com/articles/200153756) in a normal browser and save it as a PDF; direct fetches timed out for every researcher, and it was read only once through a text reader (G3; G4 gsrc-3). Confirm the copyright@take2games.com address on that page.
3. **Mon 16 Nov: write to Take-Two** at copyright@take2games.com: describe the fan channel, your own gameplay, real commentary, no spoilers, and ask whether monetised videos are allowed. Do not treat silence as a yes (G3 Risks).
4. **Mon 16 Nov: create the channel's identity** (G7 point 8; A10 checklist).
   - A new Google account with 2-Step Verification, separate from the company's account and not a Brand Account under it, so the clips system can never sign in to the company channel.
   - A name or handle with "fan" in it (the "Leonida Fan Clips" pattern); no "Rockstar", "Official" or creator names.
   - Phone-verify the channel and turn automatic dubbing off.
   - Original icon and banner art, plus the line "Unofficial fan channel. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Rockstar Games or Take-Two."
5. **Tue 17 Nov: create the Cloud project from that new account**, OAuth consent "External" and "In production", not attached to production's billing; add a second owner to production's own Cloud project from a company account that never touches clips (A9 point 2; A14 points 2-4).
6. **Tue 17 Nov: buy only what route (a) needs** (G4 point 1; G1 gta-m11).
   - A PS5 or Xbox Series X|S if you have none (not Xbox One cloud play); price it locally.
   - The game, $79.99 standard edition.
   - An Elgato Game Capture 4K S ($159.99), which records to a Windows PC with OBS, or start with the free PS5 capture to a USB stick.
   - An external drive; 1080p recording is about 5.4 GB an hour (estimate, G4 gsrc-23).
   - Do not buy: a residential proxy, a Hetzner or Contabo plan, or anything that charges to join a campaign (A12; G2 money-17).
7. **Wed 18 Nov: write to 5 GTA creators** (GTA Series Videos, MrBossFTW, DarkViperAU first) using the sample message in G4, but change its request: ask them to send the files or make your account a Twitch channel editor, because downloading from YouTube also needs YouTube's own permission (A3 point 3; G8 gingest-m1). Save every reply with its date (G4).
8. **Wed 18 Nov: set the AI and server guards.** Create a separate Anthropic organisation or workspace limit; on AWS, check the instance's credit mode and keep it apart from production (A12 host-18, host-m12).
9. **Thu 19 Nov (launch day): test, do not post** (G3 Risks; G6 Risks; G8 Risks).
   - Re-read Rockstar's policy and save a dated copy.
   - Check the game's audio menu for a radio-off or streamer-safe option.
   - Record 5 minutes at the top setting and send the file for an `ffprobe` check.
   - Note any scene the console will not record.
   - Check frame rate and HUD position on 5 real gameplay videos before the templates are frozen.
10. **Fri 20 Nov: start daily recording** with commentary, radio off, free roam only, no missions. Approve the first renders in the panel. Aim for the first upload around 26-29 Nov (G1 point 1).


### Where the research is thin or disagrees

1. **Rockstar's policy text was never read cleanly.** It was read once through a text reader; one checker could not open it and relied on news reports, and the news reports differ on exact wording (G3; G4 gsrc-3, gsrc-m5).
   - Settle: your own saved PDF of the page.
2. **Take-Two's real stance on monetised gameplay is unknown.** No written grant and no documented strike on an ordinary gameplay channel were found, and the search was cut short (G3 grules-7, grules-10).
   - Settle: a written reply from Take-Two.
3. **The spoiler window differs:** 2-3 weeks (G1), 30 days (G7), 8 weeks (G5).
   - Settle: your choice (decision 5).
4. **The date gate differs:** capture date before 19 Nov local time (G3), or source published before 18 Nov 10:00 UTC (G7). The unlock time comes from news only (G1 gta-4).
   - Settle: launch-day reports, then fix one rule.
5. **Starting pace differs:** 1 a day (A1), 4-6 a day (A9), a default ceiling of 4 (A2), a cap of 6 (A19).
   - Settle: the build starts at the lowest; the ramp data decides the rest.
6. **The channel's daily upload limit has no number,** and a clip channel may never get the higher tier (A19 gap7-4; A9 api-m7).
   - Settle: the slow ramp, logging every refusal and the tier shown in Studio weekly.
7. **Render time is unmeasured,** and the estimates differ (1.7-3.4 min in G6, about 5 min in an A11 checker note).
   - Settle: time one Short per template on the real server.
8. **Audience and pay per view.** You said English, worldwide; G2 assumed a mainly Pakistani audience. No Shorts rate for South Asia exists (G2 money-m6).
   - Settle: real analytics after a few weeks.
9. **Whether AI-written commentary passes review.** No case of an AI-commentary clips channel passing or failing was found (A16 gap4-9).
   - Settle: keep a person's voice in every post until a test says otherwise.
10. **GTA 6 music.** Whether the 34 album songs or Justice's score are label-owned, and whether a streamer-safe radio exists, are unknown; the music detector may also flag engines (G3 grules-16, grules-17; G6 Risks).
    - Settle: a launch-day check of the audio menu and 30 hand-labelled clips.
11. **Console capture.** PS5 and Xbox limits come from old or vendor articles, and whether any scene blocks recording is unknown (G4 gsrc-9; G8 gingest-14, gingest-15).
    - Settle: a 5-minute test file read with `ffprobe`.
12. **Usable moments per hour of play are unmeasured,** so whether even 6 good posts a day is reachable is unknown; hourly would need about 18 source hours a day (G5 gpick-m9).
    - Settle: two weeks of a person marking the top 20 candidates as post or skip.
13. **How YouTube links channels to a person is not published,** and the reported cluster-termination system is not confirmed to run on YouTube (A13 gap1-11; A20 gap8-8).
    - Settle: ask YouTube Creator Support in writing, or one hour with a media lawyer.
14. **Interest decay rests on Steam player counts,** not YouTube views (G1 Risks).
    - Settle: vidIQ monthly views for a few GTA channels in December 2026.
15. **Twitch's terms and Developer Agreement were never read** (G8 gingest-8, gingest-m8).
    - Settle: open them in a browser before any Twitch source is used.
16. **Tax and payment.** Whether a W-8BEN treaty claim gives 0% US withholding, and which AdSense methods work if you are paid in Pakistan, are unconfirmed (G2 money-20, money-m11).
    - Settle: one session with a local tax adviser.
17. **Partner Programme details after 1 Feb 2027.** YouTube's blog does not restate the 1,000-subscriber rule or say how pending applications are judged (G2 money-2).
    - Settle: re-read the Help page in January 2027.
18. **Hosting advice differs from your choice.** A12 recommended the laptop first, then a VPS with a different provider from production; you chose AWS. Its download-blocking worry mostly falls away, because the build does not download from YouTube unless you switch that on.
    - Settle: one week of real load on the chosen instance.
19. **The 1 October 2026 originality post was never read first-hand.** Four news reports agree on its wording (A15 gap3-1, gap3-3).
    - Settle: open it signed out in a browser.

## 2. The build plan: what is on branch `clp`

### 2.1 What it does

"clips" is a separate system inside this repo. It watches sources we are allowed to use, downloads each new video, picks the moments worth posting, renders them as Shorts (vertical, under a minute) and as longer clips, and puts them in a queue. Once a day a person spends about ten minutes on a small web page approving or rejecting what is in the queue. Approved clips get a publish time and are uploaded to the clips channel as private videos that YouTube releases at that time.

It runs as its own program on its own small server, with its own data folder, its own Google account, its own Google Cloud project and its own settings file. It adds new files to the repo (`clips/`, `tests/clips/`, `deploy/clips/`) and changes nothing in the app that runs the company channel. The only existing file touched is `.gitignore`.

### 2.2 Decisions taken, and how to change them

You said "start development as soon as possible", so I took the recommended option for each choice below. Every one except the first is a setting.

| Decision | What the build does | Why | How to change it |
|---|---|---|---|
| Which sources may be clipped | Only a source with a rights record: our own footage, written permission, a creator's public permission, a clipping campaign, Creative Commons, or official material used inside the publisher's own policy. A source with no record can be listed but is never clipped or posted. | Reposting creators without permission earns nothing from YouTube ads and can end the channel and the owner's other channels (sections G2, G3, A3). | Not a setting. Add the permission to the source and it switches on. |
| Where the footage comes from | Files in a watched folder: your own recordings, or files a creator sent you. Downloading from YouTube is switched off. | YouTube's terms forbid downloading a video without YouTube's own permission, even when the creator agrees (A3, A5). | `CLIPS_YOUTUBE_DOWNLOADS=true` |
| Nothing from before the release | A video dated before 19 November 2026 is skipped, unless the source is official material. | Pre-release and leaked footage is taken down, and Take-Two goes after leaks (G3). | `CLIPS_NOT_BEFORE` |
| Who approves | A person approves every clip before it is scheduled. | You chose ten minutes a day; it also catches spoilers, music and bad cuts before they cost a strike (G1, G3). | `CLIPS_REVIEW_REQUIRED=false` |
| How often it posts | 1 post a day in the first week, rising in steps to 4 a day by week 8 (1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3, 3, 4), never more than 6 a day, at least 3 hours apart. | No source rewards volume; back-to-back posting is linked with fewer views per Short; a new channel has an unpublished daily upload limit (A1, A9). | Hourly: `CLIPS_POSTS_PER_DAY=24`, `CLIPS_MAX_POSTS_PER_DAY=24`, `CLIPS_MIN_GAP_MINUTES=60` |
| How it uploads | Private, with a publish time; YouTube makes it public. A clip whose time has passed goes back for a new slot, so nothing goes public at once. | A failed loop or a lost network can't break the timing, and nothing is public before a person has seen it (A9, A12). | `CLIPS_UPLOAD_AHEAD_HOURS` |
| Where it posts | One channel only, named in `CLIPS_CHANNEL_ID`. Any other channel is refused, and the company channel is on a refuse list. | A wrong-channel post is the one mistake that cannot be undone quietly (A11). | `CLIPS_CHANNEL_ID`, `CLIPS_FORBIDDEN_CHANNEL_IDS` |
| The look | ffmpeg only, four layouts for gameplay, hook text at the top, credit line, captions when there is speech, 1080x1920 at 30 frames a second. | GTA 6 runs at 30 frames a second on consoles; ffmpeg alone is fast enough on a small server (G6, A7). | Layout per clip on the review page; `CLIPS_OUTPUT_FPS`, `CLIPS_CAPTIONS` |
| /brag and Hyperframes | Not in this first build. | /brag makes 20-second launch videos of software projects, not clips of footage. Hyperframes can add animated overlays later; it needs Node and a headless browser on the server (A8). | A later step; see 2.8. |
| Spoilers and licensed music | Dropped by default. | Rockstar removes story reveals; in-game radio songs bring Content ID claims (G3, G6). | Per source: `avoid_spoilers`, `skip_music` |
| Lengths | Shorts 15 to 58 seconds; long clips 3 to 10 minutes. | A claimed Short over a minute is blocked (A3). | `CLIPS_SHORT_MAX_S`, `CLIPS_LONG_MIN_S`, `CLIPS_LONG_MAX_S` |
| The AI | Whatever the app is set to: Claude Sonnet by default; Gemini works by setting `LLM_PROVIDER=gemini`. | You said most likely Claude Sonnet, maybe Gemini. Picking costs a few cents per source hour (G5). | `LLM_PROVIDER`, `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`, `GEMINI_MODEL` |

### 2.3 How it is put together

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `clips/models.py` | The shared data shapes: source, video, moment, clip, and the list of rights bases. |
| `clips/config.py` | The settings (all start with `CLIPS_`), read from `.env.clips`. |
| `clips/store.py` | One SQLite file holding sources, videos, clips, an event log and a few flags. |
| `clips/rights.py` | The rights rules: which basis needs which evidence, and the last check before an upload. |
| `clips/sources.py` | Adding, enabling and disabling sources. Enabling is refused without a valid rights record. |
| `clips/watch.py` | Finds new videos: a YouTube channel's uploads, or files dropped into a watched folder. |
| `clips/fetch.py` | Gets a video onto disk at up to 1080p, with its "most replayed" graph, chapters and captions. |
| `clips/signals.py` | Cheap clues to good moments: loud peaks, bursts of scene changes, the replay graph. |
| `clips/llm.py` | Calls the language model the app is configured for. |
| `clips/pick.py` | Chooses the moments and checks them (length, overlaps, spoilers, music). |
| `clips/layouts.py`, `clips/captions.py`, `clips/render.py` | Build and run the ffmpeg commands for Shorts and long clips. |
| `clips/package.py` | Writes the title, description, hashtags and tags, and checks them. |
| `clips/slots.py` | Works out the next free publish times from the pace settings. |
| `clips/guard.py` | The brakes: data-folder check, channel check, kill switch, breaker. |
| `clips/uploader.py` | Signs in to the clips channel and uploads, at most once per clip. |
| `clips/runner.py`, `clips/__main__.py` | The loop and the command line (`python -m clips ...`). |
| `clips/api.py`, `clips/web/index.html` | The review page and its API. |
| `deploy/clips/` | Dockerfile, compose file, example settings and the set-up steps for a separate server. |
| `tests/clips/` | The tests. Nothing in them touches the network or needs a key. |

### 2.4 The flow

1. **Watch.** For each enabled source with a valid rights record, list its new videos. Videos that fail the per-video check (for example a Creative Commons source with a video that is not Creative Commons) are saved as skipped, with the reason.
2. **Process.** For each new video: download it, find candidate moments from the cheap clues, let the model choose the best ones, drop spoilers and music, render each as a Short or a long clip, write its title and description, and save it as a draft.
3. **Review.** A person opens the page, watches each draft, edits the title if needed, and approves or rejects it.
4. **Schedule.** Each approved clip gets the next free publish time under the pace settings.
5. **Upload.** Shortly before its time, each scheduled clip is uploaded private with its publish time. Every brake is checked first.
6. **Loop.** `python -m clips loop` repeats steps 1, 2, 4 and 5 every 15 minutes. One failed step never stops the loop.

### 2.5 The safety rails

- **Rights record.** Checked when a source is enabled, when its videos are listed, before a video is processed, and again right before an upload. There is no override.
- **Channel guard.** Before every upload the signed-in channel's id must equal `CLIPS_CHANNEL_ID` and must not be on the refuse list.
- **Own data folder.** The program refuses to run on a folder that looks like the company app's data, and refuses to upload unless the app parts it reuses are pointed at the clips folder.
- **Kill switch.** One button on the page, or `python -m clips kill`, stops everything until `resume`. Clips that are already uploaded and waiting for their time are set back to private, so they do not go out while the switch is on.
- **Breaker.** A copyright strike or claim, or three failed uploads in a row, stops uploads until a person resets it.
- **At most once.** A clip is never uploaded twice, even after a crash in the middle of an upload.
- **No tricks.** Nothing in the renderer is meant to dodge copyright matching.

### 2.6 The main settings

| Setting | Default | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| `CLIPS_STORAGE_DIR` | `storage-clips` | The clips data folder. `STORAGE_DIR` must be set to the same folder. |
| `CLIPS_API_TOKEN` | empty | The key for the review page. Set it on the server. |
| `CLIPS_CHANNEL_ID` | empty | The clips channel. Nothing uploads while this is empty. |
| `CLIPS_FORBIDDEN_CHANNEL_IDS` | empty | Channels that must never receive a post. Put the company channel's id here. |
| `CLIPS_YOUTUBE_DOWNLOADS` | false | Whether videos may be downloaded from YouTube. Off: footage comes from watched folders only. |
| `CLIPS_NOT_BEFORE` | `2026-11-19` | Videos dated before this are skipped (official material excepted). Empty switches the check off. |
| `CLIPS_POSTS_PER_DAY` | 1 | The daily allowance never drops below this. |
| `CLIPS_RAMP_STEPS` | `1,2,2,3,3,3,3,4` | Posts a day in week 1, week 2, and so on after the first post. |
| `CLIPS_MAX_POSTS_PER_DAY` | 6 | The allowance never passes this (up to 24). |
| `CLIPS_MIN_GAP_MINUTES` | 180 | The shortest time between two posts. |
| `CLIPS_TIMEZONE` | `America/New_York` | The time zone of the posting window. |
| `CLIPS_REVIEW_REQUIRED` | true | A person approves each clip. |
| `CLIPS_SHORTS_PER_VIDEO` / `CLIPS_LONG_PER_VIDEO` | 3 / 1 | How many clips to take from one source video. |
| `CLIPS_VISION` | false | Let a vision model look at frames of candidate moments. |
| `CLIPS_LOOP_MINUTES` | 15 | How often the loop runs. |

The full list, with every default, is in `deploy/clips/env.example`.

### 2.7 How it was built and tested

It was built on 14 November 2026 by a team of AI agents working in parallel. Nine builders (Claude Sonnet) each wrote one group of modules at the same time, against one shared contract. An integrator made the modules work together. Three reviewers (Claude Opus) then read the result line by line: one for safety, one for correctness, one for fit with the research. Three fixers worked through what they found. One more builder added the four changes the research summary asked for. A last reviewer checked every fix and the safety rules end to end, and a final pass fixed what that reviewer found and ran everything.

**What the reviews found.** 38 findings: 11 that had to be fixed, 24 that were worth fixing, 3 notes. The last reviewer confirmed all 11 were fixed at the root with tests, then found 4 more; those are fixed too. The ones that mattered most:

- Two programs running at once (the loop and the web page) could have uploaded the same clip twice. An upload is now claimed in the database first.
- Clips from a source that was switched off afterwards could still be approved and scheduled. Every step now checks the source again.
- The loud-moment and scene-change clues were worked out but never passed to the picker.
- A clip whose publish time had passed could have gone public at once. It now goes back for a new slot, and uploads are always private with a time at least 15 minutes ahead.
- The language model was never connected outside the tests, so the real program would have picked moments and written titles without it.
- Pressing Stop did not reach clips already uploaded and waiting for their time. Stop now sets them back to private.
- The server set-up had no place for the watched folder. It now mounts a `clips-inbox` folder.

**Tests.** 480 clips tests pass. The whole repo's test suite passes with clips in it: 2,440 passed, 2 skipped (both outside clips). `ruff check .` is clean. Of the app's existing files, only `.gitignore` and `.dockerignore` changed (a few added lines each).

**Real runs on this laptop**, with ffmpeg 9.0.1:

- A 100-second test recording was dropped into a watched folder. The real program found it, cut it into 2 Shorts and rendered both in 28 seconds.
- Both showed up on the review page in a browser. Approving one moved it to the schedule. The page logged no errors.
- A source with no rights record was refused: "No rights basis is recorded, so this source can be listed but never clipped or posted."
- Rendering an 18-second Short takes 5 to 8 seconds here, in each of the three layouts tried.

**Not tested for real.** Be clear about these before relying on it:

- An upload to YouTube. No clips channel exists yet, so uploads are tested against a fake channel only.
- The Docker image and compose file. They were written and checked by reading, never built or started.
- The picker and the title writer with a real language model. Tests use a fake one, and the laptop run used the fallback that works without a model, so its titles were plain ("GTA 6: A stretch of gameplay-test").
- Real GTA 6 footage. The game is not out. Layouts, the music flag and the spoiler flag are untuned.
- Downloads from YouTube. They are off by default and were only tested against a fake.

### 2.8 What is not built yet

- **A person's voice.** The research says real commentary by a person is what YouTube's reviewers look for before they pay a channel (G3, A16). The system cuts, frames and captions footage; it has no step yet for recording or mixing in a voice track.
- **Twitch and Kick as sources.** Their official tools only give files to a channel's own editors, so this waits until a creator makes you an editor (G8).
- **Music detection.** For now the reviewer catches radio music; the setting only drops moments the model flags.
- **Vision picking by default.** It is built but off; turn it on once there is real footage to tune it on (G5).
- **Animated overlays with Hyperframes.** Section A8 has the design and a one-hour experiment that would prove or kill it.
- **Learning from results.** Reading each clip's numbers back from YouTube and feeding them to the picker (A6).
- **Other platforms.** The one live GTA 6 clipping campaign found pays on TikTok and Instagram only (G2), so cross-posting is the next thing to build if you take that route.
- **Word-accurate captions.** Captions use YouTube's sentence timings; real word timings need a speech-to-text step (A5).

### 2.9 Your steps before the first post

Only you can do these. The set-up guide with every click is `deploy/clips/README.md`.

1. **Get at least one source you are allowed to clip.** This is the step everything else waits for. The research found three that can work: a creator who says yes in writing and sends you the files (section G4 has a short message you can send), a paid clipping campaign that supplies the footage, or your own recordings if you later get a console. The files go into a folder the system watches. Rockstar's own trailers may be used for news and commentary only.
2. **Make a new Google account** that has no role on the company channel, and create the clips channel with it. Verify the channel by phone.
3. **Make a new Google Cloud project** on that account, switch on the YouTube Data API, create an OAuth client, and move the consent screen out of "Testing" (in Testing, the sign-in expires every 7 days).
4. **Start a small server** apart from the production one, copy `deploy/clips/env.example` to `.env.clips`, fill it in, and start it with `docker compose`.
5. **Open the page, connect the channel, and add your first source** with its rights record.
6. **Spend ten minutes a day** on the review page.

### 2.10 How to run it on this laptop

From the `clp` folder, with the settings in a `.env.clips` file:

```bash
python -m clips init
```

```bash
python -m clips status
```

```bash
uvicorn clips.api:app --port 8091
```

```bash
python -m clips loop
```

## 3. Research on GTA 6 and gaming footage

- G1. GTA 6: the launch and the content wave
- G2. How a GTA 6 clips channel can earn, and how much
- G3. Rights and rules for GTA footage and for other creators' clips
- G4. Where GTA 6 footage can come from, and which channels to clip
- G5. Picking the moments in gameplay and streams
- G6. The look of a gaming Short, and rendering it with ffmpeg
- G7. Titles, hashtags and channel identity for a GTA 6 channel
- G8. Getting footage from streams and from our own recordings

### G1. GTA 6: the launch and the content wave

**The short answer.** GTA 6 comes out in 5 days, on Thursday 19 November 2026, on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S only. There is no PC version and no online mode at launch, and pre-loading has been open since 10 November (gta-1, gta-2, gta-4, gta-6, gta-7). The wave is real but front-loaded. Rockstar's own channel jumped from about 8-10M views a month early in 2026 to about 100M in October 2026 (gta-10). In comparable launches, interest in month 2 fell to roughly 25-48% of month 1, and by month 3 to roughly 8-24% (gta-14, gta-15). Big established GTA channels already own the generic formats, and even they get few views re-posting official material (gta-11, gta-12). The launch hype did not even lift a 4.14M-subscriber GTA channel's subscriber count in 2026 (gta-m7), so a new channel should plan for small numbers and a slow climb, not a share of Rockstar's 100M-a-month wave. A new channel cannot be ready on 19 November with anything safe to post. Its realistic window is weeks 2-8, with formats it makes itself from its own console capture plus a person's commentary. The "clip other GTA creators every hour" idea runs into the reach and monetisation rules covered in sections A1 and A2 (growth-4, clips-1). GTA content has stayed valuable for years, though the GTA V tail is shrinking and GTA 6 has no online mode at launch, which favours a slower, original channel over a rushed one (gta-13, gta-14, gta-m10). Even own console capture is monetised only on Take-Two's tolerance, not on a written grant (gta-m6).

#### What we found

##### 1. The official facts the channel must be built around

- Rockstar's official GTA VI page says "Coming November 19, 2026" and lists PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, with "Plays Best On" PlayStation 5 (gta-1).
- The same page shows a "Pre-Order Now" and a "Pre-Load Now" button. It lists three products: the Ultimate Edition, the Vintage Vice City Pack (a pre-order bonus) and The Vice City Collection (a collector's box). It names no PC version and no online mode (gta-1).
- Newswire posts listed on that page: "Grand Theft Auto VI Pre-Load Begins on November 10" (3 November 2026), "Explore the Grand Theft Auto VI Launch Gallery" (5 November 2026) and "Pre-Load Grand Theft Auto VI Now" (10 November 2026) (gta-1).
- Take-Two's results release of 9 November 2026 lists GTA VI for "PS5, Xbox Series X|S" on "November 19, 2026". Its CEO says the launch "is ten days away" and that pre-orders keep reaching "unprecedented levels". No PC version is listed (gta-2).
- The date has slipped twice. It was first a 2025 window, then 26 May 2026 (announced May 2025), then 19 November 2026 (announced November 2025) (gta-3). Pre-loading is already open and boxed copies shipped on 12 November, so a further delay now looks unlikely. That is our reading, not a statement from Rockstar.
- Pre-load opened on 10 November 2026: at midnight local time on PS5 and at 00:00 GMT on Xbox. It needs up to 212 GB of free space; Microsoft's store listing puts the Xbox download at about 225 GB, which matters for capture-console storage (gta-m2). Per news reports, the game unlocks at midnight local time on 19 November (gta-4). We could not open Rockstar's own Pre-Load FAQ to check the unlock time (see Risks).
- Boxed copies hold only a download code, with no disc, and reached shops on 12 November 2026 (gta-4, gta-5). Wikipedia says the code-only box helps prevent leaks and reselling. That reason is not stated by Rockstar on any page we opened (gta-16).
- The game is also playable through Xbox Cloud Gaming, including on Xbox One. Remote Play works on both PlayStation and Xbox (gta-4). On Xbox One it is cloud streaming only, at Series S settings, so capture should come from a native PS5 or Series X|S (gta-m11).
- Prices: $79.99 for the standard edition and $99.99 for the Ultimate Edition. Pre-orders opened at midnight local time on 25 June 2026 (gta-5).
- There is no online mode at launch. Rockstar's June 2026 pre-order post called the game a "single-player experience". No date for an online mode has been announced (gta-6). For comparison, GTA Online came out on 1 October 2013, two weeks after GTA V (gta-19).
- There is no PC version. None had been announced as of 11 November 2026 (IBTimes). Wikipedia says no Windows release was scheduled as of October 2026 and that "industry sources" reported a PC date of Q1 2027 in October 2026; this is unconfirmed and comes from Wikipedia only (gta-7). For GTA V, the PC version came 19 months after the console version: 17 September 2013 on console, 14 April 2015 on PC (gta-19).
- Rockstar confirmed in August 2026 that the game runs at 30 frames per second on both consoles at launch. This comes from Wikipedia's summary; we did not open the primary source (gta-8).
- We found nothing official on streaming rules, spoilers, a review embargo or launch-day capture limits. The official pages we opened say nothing on these subjects. Rockstar's video policy page on its support site would not open (see Risks). The /VI page links no creator or streaming policy, and its Downloads section offers official videos and screenshots to "download and share" with no stated terms (gta-m5). Take-Two's terms (28 February 2025) license the game for "personal, non-commercial enjoyment", bar commercial exploitation without separate written terms, and treat gameplay clips and livestreams as Custom Content usable "only as authorized by us" (gta-m6).

##### 2. How big the wave is

- Trailer 1 (4 December 2023) drew about 93M YouTube views on its first day and 101M within two days (gta-9). Trailer 2 (6 May 2025) drew 475M views in 24 hours, counted across several platforms. Rockstar gave that figure to The Hollywood Reporter, so it is not a YouTube-only number (gta-9).
- vidIQ estimates on 14 November 2026 put the official Rockstar Games channel at 14M subscribers. They put Trailer 1 at 303.35M views, Trailer 2 at 188.16M, the Launch Trailer (15 October 2026) at 79.05M, "An Extended Look" (28 August 2026) at 36.58M and "Pre-Load Now" (10 November 2026) at 12.3M (gta-10).
- Rockstar's monthly views rose from 7.7-10.0M (January-April 2026) to 64.0M in August and 100.4M in October 2026. It had 99.2M views in the last 28 days (gta-10). The bumps line up with official releases: the August extended look and the October launch trailer (gta-10, gta-20). June 2026 also had +40.26M views, which lines up with the pre-order and price reveal, so official announcements and not only trailers drive spikes; a future online-mode or PC announcement could do the same (gta-m4).
- The extended look premiered on Netflix hours before it reached YouTube, and Netflix and Twitch both had technical trouble from the demand (gta-20).
- Pre-order numbers are third-party estimates only. Wikipedia reports 6.45M pre-orders (about $630M) in October 2026, "revised to 9.69 million units in November", without naming an estimator. Sensor Tower is cited only for 89% of pre-orders being the Ultimate Edition. Take-Two and Rockstar have released no pre-order numbers (gta-18).
- GTA V earned $1 billion in its first three days (gta-19).

**How fast interest fell after other giant launches.** We found no public week-by-week YouTube viewing data for these games, and Google Trends cannot be read with our tools. As a stand-in we used monthly average concurrent players on Steam, which tracks interest in the game but is not YouTube views (gta-14, gta-15):

| Game (Steam launch month) | Month 1 avg players | Month 2 | Month 3 | Month 3 as share of month 1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Elden Ring (Mar 2022) | 522,066 | 211,469 (-59%) | 90,047 (-57%) | about 17% |
| Black Myth: Wukong (Aug 2024) | 970,443 | 332,832 (-66%) | 92,080 (-72%) | about 9% |
| Hogwarts Legacy (Feb 2023) | 270,553 | 67,680 (-75%) | 21,935 (-68%) | about 8% |
| GTA V PC (Apr 2015) | 192,714 | 93,362 (-52%) | 46,953 (-50%) | about 24% |

(Shares are our arithmetic.) We did not get data for Red Dead Redemption 2 or Cyberpunk 2077 in this session.

- GTA is the exception on the long tail, but the tail is eroding. GTA V still averaged 47,173 players on Steam in October 2026, 11.5 years after its PC launch (gta-14), down about 42% from 80,874 in January 2026, and its tail includes GTA Online, which GTA 6 lacks at launch (gta-m10). DarkViperAU drew about 125.6M views in the last 28 days and about 1.31B in January-October 2026 (vidIQ estimate, our sum). Its top videos are GTA V content, but the page does not split 2026 views by game, back catalogue or Shorts, and its latest upload (12 November 2026) had 74.86K views. It is one long-established personality channel, so it shows survivorship, not what a new channel can reach (gta-13, gta-m8).

##### 3. Which GTA videos get views, and which an automatic clipper can make

Evidence from the biggest GTA channels (vidIQ, 14 November 2026):

- GTA Series Videos (created 2007, 4.14M subscribers, 6,379 videos). Its top videos are a GTA 5 full walkthrough in 4K (16.44M views), full walkthroughs of the remastered older games (3.3-4.0M), "All Endings" (3.93M) and "All Random Events" (3.08M). Monthly views held flat at 10.1-15.2M through all of 2026 despite the GTA 6 hype, and it gained only +10K or zero subscribers a month, zero in August and October (gta-12, gta-m7).
- DarkViperAU's top GTA V videos are a no-damage run (9.9M), a glitches-and-plot-breaking compilation (7.35M), a story and lore deep dive (5.21M) and a pacifist challenge series (4.46M) (gta-13). Each one shows thousands of hours of a person's own play and commentary.
- Re-posting official trailers does not work, even for a big channel. GTA Series Videos' "GTA 6 - Pre-Load Trailer" had 47.67K views after 3 days 10 hours. A Rockstar video titled "Pre-Load Now" had 2.32M in the same span (gta-11). Caveat: the main Rockstar "Pre-Load Now" shows 12.3M in total, so the two are probably different uploads (for example a Short and a long video), the "same material" is assumed from titles, and this is one data point, an illustration and not proof (gta-m9). If anything the gap may be larger than shown.

Our reading of the formats. These are estimates from the evidence above plus sections A1 and A2, not a study.

| Format | When it peaks | Can an automatic system make it? | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Trailer re-posts and breakdowns | Before launch | No (and pointless) | The official channel wins (gta-11), and it means re-using Rockstar footage (rights: see the rules strand) |
| News and "what we know" | Before launch and week 1 | Partly: script from official pages, but needs a voice and visuals we have rights to | Facts change daily; wrong facts hurt |
| Funny moments, physics, chases, fails | Weeks 1-8, long tail | Partly: auto-detect moments in our own capture (see G5), but a person must add the joke or commentary | Strongest Shorts format; most crowded |
| Glitches and easter eggs | Weeks 1-12 | No: someone has to find them in play | High value; fast-moving race |
| Guides (money, missions, collectibles, all endings, random events) | Weeks 1-12, then evergreen | Partly: long walkthroughs are mostly raw play (gta-12) | Long-form evergreen; needs full play-throughs |
| Comparisons with GTA V, Vice City versus real Miami | Weeks 1-6 | Partly: side-by-side template with our own capture | A narrow angle a new channel could own |
| Challenges, lore deep dives | Months 2+ | No | Built on one person's long effort (gta-13) |
| Roleplay | After a PC version | No | GTA V roleplay grew on PC; no GTA 6 PC version has been announced (gta-7) |

##### 4. The competition

- Established GTA channels already have the audience and years of back catalogue: Rockstar 14M subscribers (gta-10), GTA Series Videos 4.14M (gta-12) and DarkViperAU 2.34M (gta-13). General gaming giants such as Typical Gamer (16.1M) and VanossGaming (26M) cover GTA when it is hot. Our check of their current top videos found none about GTA, so this is our observation only and not a numbered finding.
- We could not measure the flood of new GTA 6 channels: there is no public count, and our search budget ran out. Part A2 shows that most new channels stay small (clips-20).
- What a new channel cannot win: launch-day speed against teams that pre-loaded on 10 November, official-trailer traffic (gta-11), and reach for clips of other creators (growth-4).
- What a new channel might win, as hypotheses to test, not findings: a narrow, repeatable angle such as GTA 6 versus GTA V, Vice City versus real Miami, or guides for one activity. Another option is commentary in a language big channels ignore, such as Urdu or Hindi, which fits the owner's likely region. Clips on a fixed daily schedule help too, but only with our own commentary.

##### 5. Risks peculiar to GTA

- **Leaks.** Take-Two filed takedowns of YouTube videos after the September 2022 leak. In August 2026, after the "CyberLeek" leak of the map and footage, it filed subpoenas against Discord, Microsoft and X Corp to identify the leaker. More material leaked in October 2026, including nude footage that likely came from a debug mode (gta-16). Per Wikipedia, the subpoenas covered the Discord server of the streamer DarkViperAU, and Rockstar acknowledged the leaks on 26 August 2026, so enforcement has reached creator communities (gta-m3). Any clip of leaked material is a takedown magnet, and per hard rule 9 we never use it.
- **Age restriction.** YouTube generally does not remove video-game violence when it is clearly a game. It may age-restrict graphic scenes such as torture, dismemberment, decapitation or mass violence against non-combatants, including in video games. A video that "focuses solely on the most graphically violent part" of a game is one factor it weighs (gta-17). Age-restricted videos are shown only to signed-in viewers aged 18 or over, are hidden from some parts of YouTube and "may also have limited or no ads" (gta-17). An automatic picker that chases "intense" moments will pick exactly these scenes.
- **Ads (advertiser-friendly rules).** These matter more for revenue than age restriction. Unedited gameplay violence is "generally acceptable", but "montages where gratuitous violence is the focal point" are not. Graphic game violence in the thumbnail or in the first 7 seconds earns no ad revenue, and in the thumbnail alone earns limited ads. Also no ads: mass-killing of non-playable characters, gameplay "manufactured to create a shocking experience", graphic torture and sexualised game content. A Short that opens on its most violent beat, or a chaos or kill compilation, hits these rules directly (gta-m1; other sections cite the same page).
- **Another delay.** Unlikely now that pre-load is open (gta-1, gta-4). It is still a reason not to sink money before 19 November.
- **Console-only capture.** Until a PC version exists, every frame we own must come from a PS5 or Xbox, or from Xbox Cloud Gaming (gta-4, gta-7). Whether Rockstar blocks console recording in some scenes is unknown; see G8. PC mods and roleplay wait for a PC version, possibly months away (gta-7, gta-19).

#### What this means for our build

1. **Do not aim for 19 November.** In 5 days the clp branch cannot be built, tested and connected to a new channel safely. Missing day 1 costs less than a strike: the drop from month 1 to month 2 is about 50-75% (gta-15), and the GTA tail has lasted years, though it is shrinking (gta-13, gta-14, gta-m10). Target the first upload by about day 7-10 (26-29 November 2026) and full rhythm by day 14.
2. **Make our own footage the default source.** Our own capture of the game with our own commentary is the best source we have, but owning the capture is not owning the rights: Take-Two's terms allow only personal, non-commercial use unless it authorises more in writing, so monetising gameplay rests on Take-Two's tolerance (gta-m6). That needs a native PS5 or Xbox Series console, the $79.99 game (gta-5) and a capture path (see G8). Clips from other creators stay off by default (growth-4, clips-1). Rockstar's own rules on posting and monetising gameplay are still unread (gta-m5), so the rights strand (G3) must confirm them before the first upload. Plan for small numbers and a slow climb (gta-m7, gta-m8).
3. **Pre-launch material.** Before 19 November we have nothing we clearly have rights to except our own words and graphics. Do not re-post or cut up official trailers: the official channel wins those views anyway (gta-11), and the rights are unclear. If anything goes out before launch, make it a text-and-graphics Short built from facts on official pages (date, platforms, pre-load size), each with its source. Making these is optional; they cost little.
4. **Source frame rate.** The game runs at 30 fps (gta-8). Render Shorts at 30 fps so frames are not invented or duplicated.
5. **Picker rules.** Penalise or block gore-heavy and nudity-heavy moments so videos avoid age restriction and reduced ads (gta-17). Also enforce the ad rules: no Short or thumbnail that opens on graphic violence in the first 7 seconds, and no chaos or kill compilations or mass-NPC-killing scenes (gta-m1). Never accept material whose origin is unknown, or footage dated before 19 November that is not official (leak risk, gta-16).
6. **Formats to support first.** (a) 30-60 s vertical Shorts of funny moments, physics, chases and fails from our own play, with a commentary track or a written punchline added by a person. (b) Side-by-side comparisons (GTA V versus GTA 6, game versus real place). (c) One weekly long video of 8-20 min, such as a guide or "every X in GTA 6". Leave glitch-hunting, challenges, lore and roleplay to a person or to later.
7. **A person approves every upload** during the first 30 days. Facts change fast at launch, and the age-restriction and leak risks need human eyes.
8. **First 30 days in outline (our proposal, not a finding):**
   - 14-19 November: owner decisions; buy hardware and the game; create the channel on a separate Google account (see A2); start on the branch.
   - 19-25 November: play and record daily; build capture ingest, the picker and Shorts templates; no uploads yet, or only optional fact Shorts.
   - 26 November to 3 December: 1 Short a day plus 1 long video; check stayed-to-watch at 48 hours (see A1).
   - 4-18 December: up to 2-3 Shorts a day if retention holds; 1-2 long videos a week; double down on the angle that wins.
   - Watch for an online-mode announcement (gta-6) and a PC announcement (gta-7). Each is a second wave with new formats.

#### Risks and unknowns

- **Rockstar's video policy is unread.** support.rockstargames.com timed out three times, both for the Pre-Load FAQ and for the policy page on posting Rockstar material. Whether Rockstar allows monetised gameplay videos of GTA VI, and on what terms, is not confirmed in this section. Cheap check: open the page from a normal browser, or see the rights strand.
- **Not confirmed: $942M pre-order figure and Sensor Tower's 9.69M estimate.** No opened source gives them; the claim was removed and replaced with the third-party estimates above (gta-18).
- **Checker disagreement.** One checker confirmed the DarkViperAU claim that GTA V content still draws huge views; the other found the source gives no per-game split. We kept the more cautious reading (gta-13).
- **vidIQ per-video numbers are rough.** Rockstar's "Pre-Load Now" shows 12.3M in total and 2.32M at 3 d 10 h, probably two uploads (gta-m9).
- **Unlock time.** "Midnight local time on 19 November" comes from news (gta-4), not from a Rockstar page we opened.
- **No YouTube decay data.** We have Steam player counts as a stand-in (gta-14, gta-15). Console-only GTA 6 may behave differently, and Steam data covers only PC players. Cheap check: once we have a channel, Studio analytics; before that, vidIQ monthly views for a few GTA channels in December 2026.
- **The new-channel flood is unmeasured.** Our web search budget ran out partway through this strand, so the count of new GTA 6 channels and the evidence on Urdu or Hindi GTA content are missing. Cheap check: a YouTube search for "GTA 6" filtered to this week, counting channels under 30 days old.
- **vidIQ numbers are estimates** from public counts that YouTube rounds (see A2, clips-m5).
- **Wikipedia-sourced facts** (gta-3, gta-8, gta-9, gta-16, gta-19, gta-20) are secondary. The page cites primary reporting, which we did not open.
- **Spoilers.** We found no official spoiler or embargo rule. Story spoilers in titles or thumbnails may draw dislikes and reports (our estimate). Keep story spoilers out of titles and thumbnails for the first 2-3 weeks.
- **Instructions inside pages.** None of the pages we opened tried to instruct us.
